header: WHAT THE CARD IS TOLD ABOUT A TRAIN'S FARES: the saved ones, from the database only, always with the time they were received. I never let the app ask RailRadar's fare service: the plant pays for it for one month only, so I collected the fares into the database (scripts/harvest-fares.ts, scripts/harvest-legs.ts), and after the month the database is all there is. A train with no saved row has no fares and the card says so.
* Before the end of the paid month I show the saved row as it is; the collection scripts may refresh it, the app never does.
* From the day after FARES_LIVE_UNTIL I mark the rows "frozen": they are no longer refreshed.

symbols.name: FARES_LIVE_UNTIL
doc: The last day on which the fare service is asked. The paid month renews on 14 Dec 2026, so I stop the day before and never rely on a renewal.

symbols.name: FareAnswer

members.name: frozen

symbols.name: legsAnswer
symbols.sig: export function legsAnswer(number: string, rows: LegRow[], now: DateTime, until?: string): LegsAnswer | null
doc: Turns the saved stops of a train into one answer; null when none is saved. I read from the database only: the stops are collected by scripts/harvest-legs.ts and never asked for by a click (a long-distance train has 50 stops and 200 requests).

behaviours: the paid fare service is open to the end of 13 Dec 2026 (Indian time) and closed from 14 Dec; the renewal day is never relied on
the day is the Indian day: 11 pm on 13 Dec in London is already 14 Dec in India, so closed
fares saved a day ago are shown as they are with the time received; the database is read and nothing is written
OLD fares (two weeks) are NOT refreshed by the app while the paid month is open: the saved fares are shown with their OWN time, and nothing is saved
a train with no saved fares is an error that says so (no invented fare, no request)
a database failure is a plain message, without the database's own words
AFTER the month the fares are shown frozen with their time
from the first minute of 14 Dec the fares are frozen, even those a week old
neither the fare service nor the fare route can reach RailRadar: no ask, no target, no fetcher, no timetable load
nothing in the app (src) asks RailRadar for a fare: the asking functions are used only by the collection scripts
the legs of a train are one answer in route order, dated by the OLDEST stop (none is older), with the newest too; open service means not frozen; reservation fares are not hints
after the paid month the legs are frozen; legs that are all table hints make a hint answer; a mix is not a hint; no rows is no answer
